name: Kashmir
tagline: Heaven on Earth written in lakes and mountains

attractions.name: Dal Lake
attractions.description: The iconic 18-sq-km lake at the heart of Srinagar is Kashmir's defining image — floating gardens (rad), shikaras piled high with cut lotus and marigolds, and ornate houseboats with carved walnut interiors. A shikara ride at dawn through the floating vegetable market, watching farmers pole their gardens to the Hazratbal ghat, is one of the most extraordinary sensory experiences in India.
attractions.whyVisit: The soul of Srinagar — a living, working floating city that is utterly unlike anywhere else on Earth.
attractions.bestTime: April to October; December to January for snow-dusted houseboats
attractions.mapsSearch: Dal Lake, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Gulmarg
attractions.description: At 2,690 metres, Gulmarg — 'meadow of flowers' — is Asia's premier ski destination, home to the world's highest operational gondola (Gondola Phase II reaches 3,980 m on Apharwat Peak). In winter, the resort receives 5-10 metres of powder snowfall and attracts world-class freeriders. In summer, the emerald bowl transforms into a golf course, pony-ride meadow, and the starting point for treks to Alpather Lake and Khilanmarg.
attractions.whyVisit: Asia's best ski destination by altitude, and India's most spectacular alpine meadow in summer.
attractions.bestTime: December to March for skiing; May to September for summer activities
attractions.mapsSearch: Gulmarg, Baramulla, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Mughal Gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi)
attractions.description: Three terraced Mughal gardens staircase up the eastern shore of Dal Lake against the backdrop of the Zabarwan hills. Shalimar Bagh, built by Emperor Jahangir in 1619, is the grandest — a 600-metre cascade of chinar trees, marble fountains, and flower beds. Nishat Bagh (1633) has 12 terraces symbolising the 12 zodiac signs. The smaller Chashme Shahi ('Royal Spring'), designed for Shah Jahan, is fed by a sacred natural spring.
attractions.whyVisit: The finest Mughal garden complex outside Agra, alive with chinars, fountains, and mountain reflections.
attractions.bestTime: April to June (spring flowers); October (chinar autumn foliage)
attractions.mapsSearch: Shalimar Bagh, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Sonamarg
attractions.description: The 'Meadow of Gold,' 80 km northeast of Srinagar on the Srinagar-Leh highway, is Kashmir's most dramatic gateway valley. The Sindh River rushes past as glaciers cascade off the Thajiwas mountain. The Thajiwas Glacier, accessible by pony or a 3-km walk, is a popular summer snow excursion. The valley is also the trailhead for the Nichnai and Krishnasar Lake treks leading into the high alpine Gangabal basin.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most spectacular valley road, with a glacier, wildflower meadows, and the gateway to the Great Himalayan spine.
attractions.mapsSearch: Sonamarg, Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Pahalgam
attractions.description: At the confluence of the Aru and Lidder rivers, Pahalgam is Kashmir's most picturesque hill resort at 2,130 metres. Dense pine and fir forests, rushing mountain streams, and the high meadow of Baisaran — dubbed 'Mini Switzerland' — are the main draws. Pahalgam is also the base camp for the Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage. The Betaab and Aru valleys, used extensively as Bollywood backdrops, are spectacularly beautiful.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most beautiful riverside hill town, base for the Amarnath pilgrimage and Bollywood's favourite backdrop.
attractions.mapsSearch: Pahalgam, Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Hazratbal Shrine
attractions.description: On the northern shore of Dal Lake, the gleaming white marble Hazratbal shrine is the holiest Islamic site in Kashmir. The shrine is believed to house the Moi-e-Muqqadas, a strand of hair of the Prophet Muhammad, which is displayed publicly on key Islamic dates. The white Mughal-style dome reflected in the still waters of Dal Lake at dawn, with snow-capped Zabarwan mountains behind, is one of Kashmir's iconic images.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most revered Muslim shrine, home to a sacred relic of the Prophet, on the shores of Dal Lake.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; Eid dates for relic display
attractions.mapsSearch: Hazratbal Shrine, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Shankaracharya Temple
attractions.description: Atop a 1,100-metre-high volcanic rock that rises abruptly from the valley floor above Srinagar, this Shiva temple is one of the oldest in Kashmir, believed to date to the 9th century or earlier. The 243-step climb through pine trees is a pilgrimage in itself; the summit temple — compact, circular, and carved in dark stone — offers an unobstructed 360-degree panorama of the entire Dal Lake, Srinagar city, and the Himalayan massif.
attractions.whyVisit: The best panoramic viewpoint in Srinagar, atop a sacred Shiva temple perched on a dramatic volcanic pinnacle.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; dawn and dusk for light
attractions.mapsSearch: Shankaracharya Temple, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Yusmarg
attractions.description: Often overshadowed by Pahalgam and Gulmarg, Yusmarg (2,400 m) is a hidden Kashmir meadow of extraordinary beauty. The vast grassy plateau is fringed by dark Himalayan fir forest, crossed by the Doodhganga stream, and backed by the glaciers of the Tatakooti Peak. In May and June the meadow erupts in wildflowers — violets, buttercups, and orchids. Pony rides to Sang-e-Safed glacier and Nilnag Lake are the main activities.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most unspoiled highland meadow, far quieter than Pahalgam, with glacier day-treks from camp.
attractions.mapsSearch: Yusmarg, Budgam, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Amarnath Cave
attractions.description: At 3,888 metres in the Himalaya, the Amarnath Cave enshrines a naturally occurring ice Shivalingam believed to wax and wane with the lunar cycle. One of Hinduism's most sacred sites, the annual Amarnath Yatra draws hundreds of thousands of pilgrims on two routes — via Pahalgam (32 km) and Baltal (14 km). The high-altitude trek through glaciers, moraines, and alpine meadows to the cave is as spiritually charged as any pilgrimage in India.
attractions.whyVisit: One of Hinduism's most revered pilgrimage sites, a naturally formed ice Shivalingam at near-4,000 metres.
attractions.mapsSearch: Amarnath Cave, Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Wular Lake
attractions.description: Wular Lake, 60 km north of Srinagar, is Asia's largest freshwater lake, spreading up to 260 sq km at peak flood in summer. The Jhelum River feeds and drains it. The lake's vast reedbeds support the largest colony of migratory waterfowl in the Indian subcontinent, including bar-headed geese, mallards, pochards, and rare ferruginous ducks. Traditional wicker craftsmen of Bandipora line the lakeshore, weaving willows harvested from the water.
attractions.whyVisit: Asia's largest freshwater lake, a vast bird haven and cultural landscape of floating reed islands.
attractions.bestTime: October to March for migratory birds
attractions.mapsSearch: Wular Lake, Bandipora, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Naranag Ruins and Trek
attractions.description: In the Wangath gorge north of Srinagar, the 8th-century Naranag temple complex is Kashmir's most important and least-visited ancient monument. The ruins of two massive stone-cut Shiva temples, twin tanks, and a cluster of smaller shrines are set dramatically at the mouth of the Wangath gorge. The site is also the trailhead for the 5-day Gangabal Lake trek — one of the finest in Kashmir.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's finest ancient temple ruins, in a gorgeous gorge setting at the start of the Gangabal high-altitude trek.
attractions.mapsSearch: Naranag Ruins, Kangan, Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Lal Chowk and Old City Srinagar
attractions.description: Lal Chowk — the historic town square of Srinagar — is the commercial heart of the Kashmir valley, lined with old cinema halls, tea houses, and street vendors selling kehwa (saffron tea) and lavasa bread. Beyond it, the medieval old city of winding lanes, 16th-century wooden mosques (Jamia Masjid, Shah Hamdan shrine), and 15th-century bathing ghats reveals layers of history unique to Kashmir. Hand-embroidered pashmina and kani shawl shops line the lanes.
attractions.whyVisit: The living historic heart of Srinagar, with medieval mosques, pashmina bazaars, and the warmth of Kashmiri chai culture.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; Friday mornings at Jamia Masjid
attractions.mapsSearch: Lal Chowk, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India
attractions.imageQuery: Lal Chowk old city Srinagar Kashmir

attractions.name: Betaab Valley
attractions.description: Named after the 1983 Bollywood blockbuster Betaab filmed here, this narrow valley 15 km from Pahalgam is one of Kashmir's most breathtaking landscapes. The valley floor is a lush carpet of grass and wildflowers watered by the crystal Lidder River, flanked by forest-clad slopes rising to snowfields. The Bollywood-friendly scenery of open meadows framed by dramatic rock faces has made it one of the most-filmed valleys in Indian cinema.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most visually dramatic short valley, the Bollywood backdrop that launched a thousand film songs.
attractions.mapsSearch: Betaab Valley, Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Dachigam National Park
attractions.description: Just 22 km from Srinagar, Dachigam is the only protected habitat of the critically endangered hangul (Kashmir stag), the state animal of Jammu and Kashmir. The park's forested slopes rise from 1,700 to 4,000 metres, supporting leopards, black bears, musk deer, and a rich birdlife. The park is open for guided visits to the lower reaches, and hangul sightings are most frequent in winter when the deer descend from the snowline.
attractions.whyVisit: The last refuge of the critically endangered Kashmir stag, just minutes from Srinagar's city centre.
attractions.bestTime: November to April for hangul sightings
attractions.mapsSearch: Dachigam National Park, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Verinag Spring and Garden
attractions.description: At the base of the Banihal Pass 80 km south of Srinagar, Verinag Spring is the primary source of the Jhelum River, welling up from a deep, octagonal stone basin commissioned by Emperor Jahangir in 1620. The surrounding Mughal garden with its stone channels, terraces, and poplar avenues is in a remarkably well-preserved state. A rainbow of trout is perpetually visible in the crystal-clear spring water.
attractions.whyVisit: The most serene and least-visited Mughal garden in Kashmir, framing the crystal source of the Jhelum River.
attractions.mapsSearch: Verinag Spring, Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Gangabal Twin Lakes Trek
attractions.description: The twin alpine lakes of Gangabal and Nundkol, reached on a 5-day trek from Naranag or Sonamarg, are among the most beautiful high-altitude lakes in the Himalaya. Set in a glacial cirque at 3,500 metres below the Harmukh massif (5,143 m), the lakes reflect the snow peaks in still, jade-green water. Hindu pilgrims visit Gangabal lake during the Shravan Purnima festival to immerse the ashes of the deceased.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's finest highland trek, culminating at twin glacial lakes beneath the sacred Harmukh peak.
attractions.mapsSearch: Gangabal Lake Trek, Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir, India
attractions.imageQuery: Gangabal Lake Harmukh peak Kashmir trek

attractions.name: Patnitop
attractions.description: Perched at 2,024 metres on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in the Udhampur district, Patnitop is Jammu's premier hill station — a pine-forested plateau commanding sweeping views of the Chenab valley below. Naag Temple, the Sanasar meadow 15 km away, and paragliding above the valley are highlights. In winter, Sanasar's slopes receive reliable snowfall that supports a small ski facility, making it Jammu's answer to Gulmarg.
attractions.whyVisit: Jammu division's finest hill station, combining pine-forest views, paragliding, and winter skiing at Sanasar.
attractions.bestTime: April to October; December to February for snow
attractions.mapsSearch: Patnitop, Udhampur, Jammu and Kashmir, India
attractions.imageQuery: Patnitop hill station Jammu Jammu Kashmir

attractions.name: Vaishno Devi Shrine
attractions.description: Nestled in the Trikuta Hills at 1,560 metres near Katra in Jammu, the Vaishno Devi cave shrine is one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in the world, welcoming over 8 million devotees annually. The 13-km trek (or shorter helicopter route) to the cave passes through the Baan Ganga stream and Adhkuwari. Inside the holy cave, the goddess is represented by three natural rock formations (pindis) of Mahakali, Mahasaraswati, and Mahalakshmi.
attractions.whyVisit: One of India's most revered Shakti pilgrimage sites, drawing millions of devotees to a sacred Himalayan cave.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; Navratri (March and October) for festival atmosphere
attractions.mapsSearch: Vaishno Devi Shrine, Katra, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Tulip Garden (Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden)
attractions.description: Asia's largest tulip garden sprawls across 12 terraced hectares on the foothills of the Zabarwan Range, with Dal Lake shimmering below. Each April, over 1.5 million tulips bloom in 64 varieties — scarlet, saffron, violet, white, and striped — creating one of the most colourful spectacles in India. The 2-3 week flowering season coincides with cherry blossoms, making spring in Srinagar an unforgettable seasonal phenomenon.
attractions.whyVisit: Asia's largest tulip garden, a brief but extraordinary spectacle of 1.5 million blooms above Dal Lake each April.
attractions.mapsSearch: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India
attractions.imageQuery: Tulip Garden Srinagar Dal Lake spring

attractions.name: Gurez Valley
attractions.description: One of the most isolated and scenically stunning valleys in the Indian Himalaya, Gurez sits in the Kishanganga valley at 2,400 metres near the Line of Control, 120 km north of Srinagar. The Dards — an ancient Indo-Aryan community — inhabit villages of intricately carved wooden houses. Snow-capped Habba Khatoon Peak presides over the valley, named after Kashmir's most celebrated medieval poetess. The Kishanganga River supports wild rainbow trout.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most remote and pristine valley, home to an ancient Dardic civilisation and wild trout streams.
attractions.mapsSearch: Gurez Valley, Bandipora, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Baisaran Meadow
attractions.description: A 5-km pony ride from Pahalgam leads to Baisaran, a tilted, pine-fringed alpine meadow at 2,438 metres dubbed 'Mini Switzerland' for its remarkable resemblance to Swiss alpine scenery. The meadow is carpeted with grass and wildflowers, the pines are tall and dark, and the backdrop is pure Himalayan snowfield. Horses, ponies, and ATVs are available for hire, and it features prominently in numerous Bollywood films.
attractions.whyVisit: Pahalgam's most beloved alpine meadow, with a pine-and-snowfield panorama that rivals any scene in the Alps.
attractions.mapsSearch: Baisaran Meadow, Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, India
attractions.imageQuery: Baisaran Meadow Pahalgam pine forest Kashmir

attractions.name: Manasbal Lake
attractions.description: North of Srinagar in Safapora district, Manasbal Lake is the deepest lake in Kashmir at 13 metres and one of the most important migratory bird wintering grounds in the Kashmir valley. Thousands of greylag geese, tufted ducks, common pochards, and gadwalls crowd its lotus-studded surface from October to March. The small Jarokha Garden on the northwestern shore is a Mughal-era pleasure garden in a lovely state of serene decay.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's deepest lake and the valley's finest winter birdwatching spot, with a quietly ruined Mughal garden.
attractions.bestTime: October to March for migratory birds
attractions.mapsSearch: Manasbal Lake, Safapora, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Lolab Valley
attractions.description: The Lolab Valley in Kupwara district, 100 km north of Srinagar, is one of Kashmir's least-discovered treasures — a long, forested valley of apple orchards, clear trout streams, and meadows hemmed by forested ridges rising to 3,000 metres. The villages retain traditional Kashmiri architecture untouched by modern construction. The Shali Ganga stream, the Bandipore forest, and the small Kuttal and Nau Pora waterfalls are memorable stops.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's most overlooked valley: a perfect replica of Pahalgam's beauty with almost none of the tourist crowds.
attractions.mapsSearch: Lolab Valley, Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, India

attractions.name: Srinagar's Floating Vegetable Market
attractions.description: Before dawn each morning, vendors on narrow shikaras loaded with cabbages, lotus stems, spinach, and turnips converge on the narrow channels between the floating gardens at the north end of Dal Lake. The market dissolves within two hours of sunrise. Visited by few tourists, the experience of floating among groaning vegetable boats in the half-light, surrounded by houseboats and the silhouette of the Zabarwan hills, is pure, unrepeatable Kashmir.
attractions.whyVisit: The most authentic and atmospheric dawn experience in Srinagar, a centuries-old floating market on the lake.
attractions.mapsSearch: Dal Lake Floating Vegetable Market, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India
attractions.imageQuery: Dal Lake floating vegetable market Srinagar
